lines.trans: An industry rumor dossier already seems to be making the rounds.
What X-file?
That the agency cannot manage Cindy, we are on bad terms, her contract renewal is in jeopardy…
And that she jetted off overseas on a secret romantic trip with a chaebol heir.
Then why have you still not found her while pathetic rumors like that spread?!
Those rumors would vanish right away if we found her quickly and completed an official schedule!
There is a limit to searching quietly without word getting out, and Cindy has no close friends either…
She has never been unreachable this long—what if she really had an accident or got kidnapped…
Would it not be best to report it to the police after all?
What, so we can advertise to the whole world that Cindy vanished?!

meanings.note: Used as numeral + noun (2세?).

examples.trans: A second-generation conglomerate heir, then?

examples.text: 그럼 지금 재벌 2세랑 어디 파리 특급 호텔이라도 가 있는 거 아니야?
examples.trans: Then could she be off at some luxury hotel in Paris right now with that conglomerate heir?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + subject (X파일이).

examples.trans: An industry rumor dossier already seems to be making the rounds.
What X-file?

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this police?
I was busy today because of police.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used as noun (공식).

examples.text: 얼른 찾아서 공식 일정 소화하면 쏙 들어갈 말들인데!
examples.trans: Those rumors would vanish right away if we found her quickly and completed an official schedule!
This point about official is really important.

meanings.note: Used as purposive -게 question (광고하게?!).

examples.trans: What, so we can advertise to the whole world that Cindy vanished?!

examples.text: 우리 엄마는 영화배우 장국영 좋아했는데 아빠가 장국영이 광고하는 초콜릿 백 개씩 사다 바쳐야 엄마랑 사귈 수 있었대요.
examples.trans: My mom loved actor Leslie Cheung, and she said my dad had to bring her a hundred chocolates from his commercials just to date her.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (구질구질한).

examples.text: 그러니까 왜 그런 구질구질한 소문 나게 애를 못 찾고 있냐고!
examples.trans: Then why have you still not found her while pathetic rumors like that spread?!
It is really pathetic, messy compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (납치가).

examples.text: 이렇게까지 연락이 안 된 적이 없는데 진짜 사고가 났다든가 납치가 됐다든가…
examples.trans: She has never been unreachable this long—what if she really had an accident or got kidnapped…
This point about kidnapping is really important.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?
I want to leave right now.
How about trying to leave together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (떠도는).

examples.text: 신디야, 네가 피디랑 몸싸움을 하다가 다쳤다는 둥 별 말 같지도 않은 말들이 떠도는 모양이야.
examples.trans: Cindy, absurd rumors seem to be floating around claiming you got hurt scuffling with a producer.
An industry rumor dossier already seems to be making the rounds.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Used as bound noun + casual copula (모양이야.).

examples.text: 신디야, 네가 피디랑 몸싸움을 하다가 다쳤다는 둥 별 말 같지도 않은 말들이 떠도는 모양이야.
examples.trans: Cindy, absurd rumors seem to be floating around claiming you got hurt scuffling with a producer.

examples.text: 아 진짜 돌겠네! 돈도 없고 친구는 있는데 바쁘고 다리는 그 모양이고!
examples.trans: Oh, this is driving me crazy—no money, friends who are busy, and your leg in that state!

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + object (밀월여행을).

examples.trans: And that she jetted off overseas on a secret romantic trip with a chaebol heir.
This point about honeymoon-style getaway is really important.

meanings.note: Often carries surprise

examples.trans: Is it already all finished?
It's already midnight.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (사라질).

examples.text: 말 같지도 않은 걸 뭘 신경 써요? 오늘부터 활동 시작하면 싹 사라질 겁니다.
examples.trans: Why bother over nonsense? Once I resume promotions starting today, it will all vanish.

examples.text: 그게 분명히 차에 태워서 출발을 했는데 운전하다가 돌아보니까 사라져 있더래요.
examples.trans: Well, he swears he put her in the van and pulled out, yet when he looked back while driving she had vanished.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
Did you hear about this relationship?
I was busy today because of relationship.
Is that rumour true?
A strange rumour is going around the company.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (소화하면).

examples.text: 얼른 찾아서 공식 일정 소화하면 쏙 들어갈 말들인데!
examples.trans: Those rumors would vanish right away if we found her quickly and completed an official schedule!
Let us do that (if she fulfills) right away.
Did you hear about this reporting to police?
I was busy today because of reporting to police.

meanings.note: Used as mimetic adverb (쏙).

examples.trans: Because of you, my tears went right back inside.

examples.text: 얼른 찾아서 공식 일정 소화하면 쏙 들어갈 말들인데!
examples.trans: Those rumors would vanish right away if we found her quickly and completed an official schedule!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 아무래도 미래의 의사다 보니까 공부할 것도 많고.
examples.trans: Well, since I am a future doctor, I have a ton of studying to do.
Here the word for 'after all, naturally' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: commonly used when urging someone to act

examples.trans: We're late, so let's leave right away.
Come inside quickly before you catch a cold.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used in 연락을 하다 ('to contact') and humble 연락을 드리다.

examples.trans: I will contact you later.
I heard from my friend today.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (위험하게,).

examples.text: 에이, 이 계집애가 밤늦게 위험하게, 아무튼 정말!
examples.trans: Ugh, this girl staying out so dangerously late at night—honestly!

examples.text: 회사가 신디 핸들링을 못 한다, 사이가 안 좋다, 재계약이 위험하다…
examples.trans: That the agency cannot manage Cindy, we are on bad terms, her contract renewal is in jeopardy…
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Refers to planned events or work tasks for a day or period.

examples.trans: What is your schedule like this week?
The filming schedule changed suddenly.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (재계약이).

examples.text: 회사가 신디 핸들링을 못 한다, 사이가 안 좋다, 재계약이 위험하다…
examples.trans: That the agency cannot manage Cindy, we are on bad terms, her contract renewal is in jeopardy…
This point about contract renewal is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun (재벌).

examples.trans: A second-generation conglomerate heir, then?

examples.text: 맞네! 재벌이랑 사귀니까 위약금 따위 두렵지 않다 그러고 펑크 낸 거지!
examples.trans: That has to be it! Because she is dating a tycoon, she is unafraid of penalty fees and blew off the event!

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

meanings.note: Adverb derived from 조용하다 ('to be quiet').

examples.trans: Please speak quietly.
Walk quietly in the library.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
I want to let's get along right now.
How about trying to let's get along together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Primary everyday meaning.
Used at a bank or ATM for taking out cash.

examples.trans: I withdrew money at the bank.
I am looking for my keys.

meanings.en: to be close, on good terms
meanings.note: Used for close personal relationships; often paired with -와/과 or -하고 ('with').

examples.trans: We are very close.
Are you close with that actor?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 평소처럼 필름이 끊겨 있는 게 선배님이 바라는 해피엔딩이신 거죠?
examples.trans: So having his memory blacked out like usual is the happy ending you are hoping for, right?
Here the word for 'like usual' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (한계가).

examples.text: 말 안 나게 조용히 찾는 데는 한계가 있고요, 신디가 평소에 친하게 지내던 사람도 없고…
examples.trans: There is a limit to searching quietly without word getting out, and Cindy has no close friends either…
This point about a limit is really important.
I'm traveling overseas.
I am overseas.

meanings.note: Used as loanword noun + object (핸들링을).

examples.text: 회사가 신디 핸들링을 못 한다, 사이가 안 좋다, 재계약이 위험하다…
examples.trans: That the agency cannot manage Cindy, we are on bad terms, her contract renewal is in jeopardy…
This point about management, handling is really important.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.
